lines.line: Wake up! Wake up!
Through the blurred slits of my sleepy eyes, I see some kind of beastly grin... Oh... no, it's just Sonya's smug face.
How does she keep sneaking into my apartment? Maybe I should stop giving keys to everyone.

My body feels like it's wrapped in a straitjacket. It took me a moment to realize where I was and what I was doing here.
Today, I fell asleep at the desk.
I don't even remember when it happened - the moment I slipped into the Net... it fell out of memory, like it wasn't recorded on the tape of yesterday.
-What... What are you so happy about?
-Your grumpy face! Just kidding. Today, we're all going to the festival!
-From school? For the whole day? You're kidding!
-Oh, not at all! I already gathered all the girls; we're just waiting for you.
My arms and legs felt numb, and my neck felt disconnected-falling asleep at the desk is quite an experience.
Groaning, I crawled out from behind the computer, and Sonya ran downstairs.
-Wow, you're leaving the house before noon! Impressive...
-Aren't you coming with me?
-Today, it's probably better I stay home... I'll make sure everything's in order here, maybe dust a little with my tail...
-"In order"?! If you knock something off the table again...
Purr-purr hissed at me discontentedly, and I ran away.
Downstairs, the girls were indeed waiting - Alina and Kira. They both shouted "Hi" in unison.
-Kira, you're here too! Is your brother coming?
-Strange, he was so eager to see the festival... But in the end...
-In the end, he'll just spend the whole day online again. But... I'll sha-re the experience wi-th him!
-What? Kir isn't coming?
Sonya looked visibly upset.
-Let's make lanterns for the festival together! We can't just go empty-handed, can we?
-Good idea, except... I don't know the-se traditi-ons at all... So noth-ing will work; I won't be able to make a lantern.
-It's simple! I'll show you how.
Sonya is the jack-of-all-trades in every situation. If there's someone to teach something to, she's always the first. Even if she's not great with paper crafts herself.
-If we're making everything ourselves, we need to get some scraps, wax and paper.
-I think... I can help with the paper... I just need to run home.
-When will you be back?
-Hmm... I'll be back in no more than half an hour! The-re and back!
Kira skipped off toward her home.
-So, the rest is on us...
-What about wax and cloth?
-I... I might be able to bring it.
Alina lives nearby; I think she'll be quick.
-Okay. We'll wait for you here.
Alina also left, and Sonya and I were left alone.
-Well, I guess there's no work left for us… Mira, I'm already so bored!
-Do you want me to entertain you?
-You? You? Don't make me laugh!
-Ugh, online you could just snap your fingers… And there you go, a ready-made paper lantern. Instantly!
-Well... then we wouldn't need friends. What's the point if everything's so easy?
-At least then we could immediately launch the lanterns.
-What fun is that-sitting alone staring at your own lantern?
-You could make a clown hang himself, I swear!
Sonya finally quieted down and sat on the parapet. We're waiting.
It's really nice that they let us out of school today...
Not that school would've kept me from the festival – it's just a relief to know I can skip legally this time. Besides...
When would we have gathered like this, all together, and gone somewhere? So... it all turned out just perfectly!
-The light...
-What?
-The light in Alina's place turned on about ten minutes ago… But she's still not here. Maybe something happened?
I jumped down to the ground.
-Oh no… God, please, not this again.
-Do you think we should go check on her?
-Yeah... Alina needs constant watching. I hope Kira doesn't think we just ditched her.
With some worry, we headed to Alina's yard.
-It's so... kind of... eerie here.
-Yeah. Everything's overgrown and dark, and here... feels like a rabbit hole. And these candles...
-Why couldn't she just take the wax from here?
Sonya nodded silently, and I heard her swallow.
-Alright. There and back.
-You go first.
-No, you go first.
-Alright... Let's hold hands. We'll go together.
Holding hands, we walked through the yard to the door, climbing the musty staircase. Alina's door was open.
-Should we go in?
-It seems quiet inside... but...
I heard faint sniffles and gasps. Is she crying? Really, now?
We ran into her room, which looked more like a greenhouse, and stopped in the doorway.
-Alina, are you alright?
-Yeah, I... I'm fine.
She wiped her nose with her shirt, leaving a damp mark on it.
-Why are you crying?
-I don't know... Can I take a candle?
-You've got enough here for a thousand lanterns... Why not take one?
-They... They're in memory... of my mom...
-Uh... Is she...
-She passed away.
We froze in awkward silence.
-Well... we could take an unlit one...
-Do you think that's okay?
-Of course it is. Take it and let's go.
Sniffling, Alina pulled out fresh candles from a drawer-she took four but, after a moment's thought, put one back.
-How... how did she die?
-I hardly... remember her. But she... looked so much like me... Dad said she worked at a factory, and one day...
-She slipped and… fell into a vat of meat and... got ground into minced meat.
-And then they made dumplings out of it.
Alina covered her face with her hands and began to sob harder than before.
-The whole city ate my mom.
After somehow calming Alina down, we returned. In front of the house, an anxious Kira was waiting for us.
She was looking around, trying to see where we'd gone, clutching a few rolls of colorful crepe paper.
-The-re you are! I was starting to get worried.
We decided to head to the park-to make the lanterns, setting up the whole group on the benches.
Cutting thin metal rods, we settled right at the entrance. Sonya sat next to Kira, while I sat across from them, next to Alina.
-Look, here's how it goes. First, we make the frame and the lamp holder.
Sonya bent the rod into a circle and wound it crosswise with thread.
-Got it. Like this?
-Yep.
-Now we need to make two arches, so the dome doesn't get squished. Here...
-And finally, we cover the frame with paper.
Alina and I quietly crafted our wonder-lanterns.
Alina was much better and faster at it than all of us combined.
Her round base was somehow "rounder," the thread was wrapped tighter and more evenly; in short, an ideal festival lantern.
-Looks like we should have had Alina as the teacher. Look!
Alina blushed and looked embarrassed.
-Oh, I'm... it's nothing.
Sonya frowned and threw a wad of paper at me.
-Oh, that's not true.
Alina turned to the stack of colorful paper, then looked at me.
-What's your favorite color?
-I don't know, probably yellow.
-Alright. Then I'll take a different one.
Alina wrapped the lantern with green crepe paper and held it up.
-Here's my lantern.
-Alright, let's write our wishes on them. The lanterns will fly up into the sky... Maybe someone up there will read them.
One by one, everyone took a pencil and carefully scrawled something on the small papers attached to the balloons.

Finally, the pencil was handed to me.
What... should I write?
-Hurry, to the festival!
Today's the height of the celebration. Dancing around bonfires, lanterns, local music, drunken gangs wandering around, vomit, killings, rivers of blood-a wonderful time!
The park greeted us with round dances and songs in a strange language.
-I want to, I want to join them!
-Sonya, these are some fucking junkers, you...
Sonya pulled a stimulator out of her bag, and I immediately fell silent.
-What?
-No… Nothing. Forget it.
She joined a group of dancing girls in traditional dresses that looked more like tattered rags, and even though she stood out so much, she looked like one of those dancers.
-Look at her go...
Merging into the round dance, she disappeared from sight. I picked up the lantern she left behind.
-Should we wait for her?
-No way. Got nothing better to do.
Under an auntie's umbrella, we got some snacks-a hatch opened, and out of the cart came a sausage for a hot dog, corn, and a steamed bun.
Between the three of us, we could take bites from each other's food if we wanted to taste a bit of everything.
Along with all this, we grabbed three cans of milk soda.
I purposely didn't get anything for Sonya. She'll manage. Besides, she wouldn't want anything to eat until she's sobered up.
-Mira, why didn't you tell me they make such good food here!
-You mean the tsuki-pie?
-Is that... what it's called?
-I don't like cabbage...
-If you don't eat cabbage, your boobs won't grow.
Sonya bumped into me, knocking me down.
-Hey, what are you doing?
Sonya was unrecognizable. A madly positive expression on her face and her darting, wide-open eyes.
I instinctively recoiled.
-Miss me? HUMM!
With one bite, half the hot dog was in her mouth.
Seriously.
-Time to launch the lanterns!
Someone found a lighter in their pocket, and one by one, I struggled to light all the candles.
When the air inside the lantern heats up, it will break away from the ground and fly up to the sky with the others.
The orange glow warmly reflects off our noses and in our shiny eyes. As if on cue, everyone falls silent.
The moment before sending your wish up to the clouds.
Like when you're sitting in front of a cake with colorful candles on your birthday, wondering if you made the right wish. As if it really matters...
This would have been... the best day in a long time. If not for Sonya. She's trembling all over... Was it worth ruining everything?
The paper dome began to unfurl and inflate. It would soon soar into the air.
-Mira, what did you wish for? Tell me, tell me, I'm curious!
-Well... I...
-You probably wished to finally learn to dance, haha!
That really stung me. If not to say, she stabbed me right in the heart with that remark.
No matter how I tried to hold it in, tears welled up in the corners of my eyes.
If only she knew that...
-Oh, I knew it!
She's completely unrecognizable. As if she's gloating... as if she knows she's hurting me. Is this all just "SPAM"?
Or maybe... what's on a drunk's lips is what's on their sober mind, and... all this time...
I clenched my teeth to keep from sobbing and wiped my face with my sleeve.
The girls froze in confusion, looking at Sonya.
We had to hold onto the lanterns to keep them from flying away.
Sonya's lantern had a "wound" – a slit in the paper where all the hot air began to escape, and the lantern was descending.
-Let's launch them!
Finally, our handmade lanterns took flight. The wind made them dance, nearly colliding with each other.
-Wow, look!
We clasped our hands into fists, throwing our heads back, unable to look away.
-Fly, fly!
-How could this... whatever, fuck you all.
-What's with you? If you want to ruin the festival for everyone, then just leave!
Sonya turned and stomped off toward the midnight sun that they were preparing to ignite. A whole crowd had formed around the bales of hay arranged in a circle, and Sonya disappeared into it.
-Is she really this upset about the lantern? We need to calm her down...
-And where do we find her now?
It's like finding a needle in a haystack...
We held hands with the girls to avoid getting separated even more and dived into the boisterous crowd.

A tunnel between the drunken, smelly bodies would open briefly, allowing us to squeeze further along the circle, only to close again, and we'd have to push another body with all our might to let our little train through.
With each passing second, our hope of finding Sonya here was fading. We circled around the future bonfire site, already drenched in accelerant.
They wouldn't trample her here, right? Maybe we should just keep celebrating?
-M-Mira, look, look!
Alina pointed fearfully at Sonya, who was climbing up a nearby technical tower next to the 'midnight sun.'
-Hey, where are you going?! Get down, now!
She acted like she couldn't hear. Damn!
-Girls, I'm going after her. You two move further back, the heat from the bonfire will be intense.
-But what about you?
Some fat body, arms, legs, hats flying to the ground-I shove another body out of the way, letting out a crazed scream, and finally, I'm at the ladder.
-Girl, you're not allowed up there!
Kicking someone away, I climb up the ladder.
Sonya is standing on the metal platform, turned away.
-What are you doing? Let's get out of here before we're roasted alive!
-Why bother?
-What?
-You're just an empty shell.
-I'm not an empty shell! What are you talking about?
-And I... am an empty shell. None of this is real.
-What difference does it make what I say to you if you're just a piece of my memory?
-I could kill you... and everyone around... and then I'd just... reset the world and do everything differently.
-Endless tortures for people who aren't even real! And my...
Sonya stepped to the edge of the platform and turned to face me.
-If the one writing my script wants me to die... then... let me die.
She gently laid down bunny at my feet.
-I promised I'd give you something... Here, take it. A memento... Haha.
-What a drag...
-Bye.
Time seemed to lose its rhythm.
Sonya stepped to the edge and jumped down into the ring of hay soaked in gasoline. The scene looked like something from a film...
She seemed to hang in the air for an eternity, between me and the pile of hay.
The bonfire ignited. The flames consumed her body.
A powerful wave of heat hit my face.
-Sonya, it's... it's...
An insane scream of agony nearly burst my eardrums and tore me to pieces. She was still alive.
She's down there, in the fire. We need to... need to put it out...
People rushed around with buckets of sand and water, trying to smother the hay-but it was useless.
The fire didn't care what it consumed-human flesh or just hay.

I stood there, watching her burning silhouette writhe, her clothes melting and sticking to her equally melting skin as she fell and rose again, her body turning darker and charred, becoming a burnt corpse.
I couldn't do anything. They dragged me off the tower, and I clutched her jacket in my hands.
From the flaming hay, they pulled out a charred piece of meat that once was Sonya.
She was still breathing... despite all the burns and unimaginable pain.
-Her whole body is burned...
-A girl, a teenager... We have no more than an hour.
-Oxygen mask... here.
In the back of the vehicle, someone with sweat on their forehead filled out an examination card.
-How long to the center?
-Thirty minutes, no traffic... Just pray we make it.
-We need to put her under before she dies from shock...
-I know... But what if she doesn't wake up?
The doctor pulled a syringe filled with clear liquid from the medical bag. He looked at the paramedic holding Sonya's arm.
-Go on.
The paramedic pressed his lips together, took the syringe from the doctor's hands. A few missed tries-the hands were shaking too much... Finally, he hit the vein.
Sonya closed her eyes. Her chest barely rose, her breathing slowed.
-It's done.
The paramedic pulled out the syringe.
Sonya lay on the stretcher like a wooden doll. Her face finally looked peaceful.
They wouldn't let me into the ambulance. It sped off with dreadful sounds. I immediately fainted.
-Mira, you've been sitting in front of that silly tape recorder for an hour!
Mom is snapping at me again.
-Put it away already, this noise is unbearable!
I tried to ignore her as much as I could, burying myself in my player.
-Turn off your cassete player, I want to watch TV. Want to join me?
-I don't care about anything anymore.
-Mira, that's no reason to grieve like this! You have to live on. No one will bring back the people who leave. You just have to come to terms with it.
I want to get as far away from her as possible, so I never have to see her again. Doesn't matter where.
Pop
Something crackled in my head.
